subject: Dedicated reservation options — floor, warm pool, and phased activation (Terramed / TR-4782)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ramos <sales@terramed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-12T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated reservation options — floor, warm pool, and phased activation (Terramed / TR-4782)

Alex —

Thanks for the conversation yesterday. Attached is a compact worksheet (terramed_capacity_workbook_v1.xlsx) and three distinct reservation pathways we think map to your product roadmap and peak forecasting. High-level summary below so you have something to circulate with procurement and engineering quickly.

Context & goals
- Predictable per-token cost for inference at scale, avoiding burst throttles during clinical peak hours.
- Fast tail latency for interactive clinician UX target: p95 < 380ms.
- Capacity to support staged feature rollouts (NLP triage -> summarization -> real-time suggestions).

Option A — Conservative (low upfront commitment)
- Baseline cluster: 8 GPUs (A100-equivalent) minimum dedicated floor
- Warm pool: 4 GPUs kept prewarmed during working hours (12h local) to reduce cold-starts
- Burst path: ability to burst up to +24 GPUs from shared capacity (best-effort)
- Ramp: month 0–3 keep baseline; month 4 reassess; optional add of +8 GPUs after 6 months
- SLA: 99.5% availability on dedicated floor; latency SLO best-effort for burst
- Use-case fit: early product-market fit / constrained procurement windows

Option B — Balanced (recommended)
- Baseline cluster: 24 GPUs (A100-equivalent) dedicated
- Warm pool: 8 GPUs prewarmed 24/7, additional ephemeral warmers during night-surge windows
- Burst path: guaranteed reserved burst lane of +16 GPUs (priority routing)
- Ramp: quarter-aligned staircase: Q1 start 12 GPUs active, Q2 +6 GPUs, Q3 +6 GPUs to hit 24
- SLA: 99.9% availability on baseline + priority for burst lane; p95 latency SLO target achievable with small batching tuning
- Use-case fit: production rollout with daily active clinician traffic; good balance of cost vs reliability

Option C — Aggressive (throughput-first)
- Baseline cluster: 64 GPUs dedicated
- Warm pool: 16 GPUs hot-standby, all prewarmed 24/7
- Burst path: committed burst capacity +32 GPUs with guaranteed throughput slots
- Ramp: 30-day activation windows with capacity stubbed on contract signature
- SLA: 99.95% availability and prioritized failover; dedicated support and booking windows
- Use-case fit: full-scale national rollout, low tolerance for throttling or latency variance

Operational notes / billing mechanics
- Warm pool hours are priced as a discounted reservation component (warm-hours credit) — reduces cost compared to on-demand prewarming.
- We recommend a 12–18 month anchor for Option B to amortize prewarm credits and provide predictable burn rates.
- We can align invoice milestones to quarterly ramp steps to match your internal budget cycles.

Requested next steps
1) Tell us which option (A/B/C) you want modeled; we can deliver a 3-line item redline and updated workbook within 48 hours.
2) If procurement needs a PO template, please loop them in — we can provide a TerraMed-ready PO PDF and a DocuSign envelope.
3) Engineering: share expected peak sequence length distribution and p95 target for a final tuning pass.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the workbook.

—
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0129

Attachment: terramed_capacity_workbook_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet — capacity scenarios, monthly burn, token-cost model)
From: Alex Ramos <sales@terramed.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-13T08:17:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options — floor, warm pool, and phased activation (Terramed / TR-4782)

Neha —

Appreciate the quick breakdown and the workbook. A couple clarifying Qs from my side and procurement: 

1) SLA / latency tiers: how much incremental cost to move from 99.5 -> 99.9 -> 99.95 in Option B? Our clinicians care about tail latency for suggested edits and we want to understand the delta.
2) Warm pool: we like the warm pool model, but procurement asked whether warm pool hours can be 100% consumed as compute credits if not used (i.e., carry-forward vs lose).
3) Pilot ask: would Redwood consider a 6-week pilot at 8 dedicated GPUs (trial baseline) with the option to convert into Option B credits if we sign before pilot end? That helps our internal stakeholders justify the spend.

Also looping procurement: Procurement Team <procurement@terramed.com> — we may need a PO ready by the end of Feb if the pilot looks good.

Cheers,
Alex Ramos
Director of Product — TerraMed
alex.ramos@terramed.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-14T11:23:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Suggested tweaks for Terramed proposal (TR-4782)

Quick internal note before we send answers to Alex/procurement —

Response bullets we should send:
- SLA pricing delta: moving Option B from 99.9 -> 99.95 is ~4.2% uplift on reservation line (mainly due to guaranteed throughput lanes and preemptive warmers). 99.5 -> 99.9 is ~2.1% uplift. I'll attach a short summary to include in the external note.
- Warm-pool credits: standard is non-transferable month-to-month, but we can build a 3-month rolling credit for enterprise anchors (12+ months) — this is contractual language but often acceptable.
- Pilot conversion: propose a convertibility clause: pilot fees (6 weeks at 8 GPUs) convert 100% to credits against the first quarter of an Option B 12-month commitment if we execute within 30 days of pilot end. That makes the pilot effectively a trial with upside for TerraMed.

I drafted a short additional attachment (commitment_summary_v2.pdf) with the financial uplift numbers and the conversion language. Recommend we send a single reply that: answers the three Qs, includes the two attachments, and proposes a 30-min call mid-next-week to lock down the pilot PO.

Neha / Marissa — if you agree I can send this to Alex + procurement.

—Karthik

Attachment: commitment_summary_v2.pdf (one-page uplift math, pilot-convertibility clause)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@terramed.com>, Alex Ramos <sales@terramed.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options — floor, warm pool, and phased activation (Terramed / TR-4782)

Hi Alex / Procurement —

Thanks — looping procurement directly. Per Karthik and Neha's notes:

1) SLA / pricing: attaching the uplift summary (see commitment_summary_v2.pdf). For Option B, expect ~2.1% uplift to go from 99.5 -> 99.9, and ~4.2% to go to 99.95. We can bake exact numbers into the SO (line-level).

2) Warm pool credit policy: for a 12+ month commitment Redwood can offer a 3-month rolling credit on warm hours (unused warm-hour credits roll for up to 3 months). We'll include the contractual language in the SOW.

3) Pilot: we can do the 6-week pilot at 8 GPUs. If you convert to a 12-month Option B within 30 days of pilot end, pilot fees convert 100% to first-quarter credits.

Next steps for procurement:
- I attached a PO template (po_template_terra.pdf) and a DocuSign link for the SOW: https://app.redwood/docusign/TR-4782
- If you can confirm PO issuance target (date) we will reschedule engineering kickoff and reserve the initial warm pool windows.

Would you like a 30-min call to review the SOW and the pilot conversion language? We're available Wed/Thu next week.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
